name: Allam-Fetvedt cycle (oxy-combustion supercritical CO2 power)
applications: natural gas power with inherent capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Natural gas burns in oxygen diluted with hot recycled CO2. The high-pressure CO2 and water mixture drives a turbine, is cooled in a recuperator, and the water is condensed out. Most CO2 is recompressed and recycled; the excess is near-pure and goes straight to a pipeline.

suppliers.name: NET Power (cycle developer), Toshiba (combustor and turbine)

source.note: POWER magazine, 1 Apr 2019

advantages: Capture is inherent to the cycle; no separate capture plant
Pipeline-ready CO2
limitations: New turbine and combustor technology; first commercial plants not yet operating as of the source
Air separation unit cost and power

name: Amine solvent post-combustion capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is cooled and contacted counter-currently with an aqueous amine solution, which reacts with CO2. The CO2-rich solution is heated with low-pressure steam in a stripper, releasing a near-pure CO2 stream and regenerating the solvent for reuse. Vendors differ mainly in solvent formulation, heat integration and solvent management.

process_steps.name: Flue gas pretreatment and cooling
equipment: direct contact cooler or quench pre-scrubber

name: Calcium looping
applications: cement (purge CaO usable as raw meal)

source.note: Energy & Fuels 38(15), 2024, CC BY 4.0: pilot at TRL7; IEAGHG 2019 gave TRL 6

principle: Lime (CaO) captures CO2 from flue gas in a carbonator at about 650 °C, forming CaCO3. The solids circulate to a calciner at about 900-950 °C, fired with fuel in oxygen and CO2, which releases a concentrated CO2 stream and regenerates CaO. Fresh limestone is added to make up for sorbent decay.

process_steps.name: Heat recovery, CO2 purification and compression

key_equipment: two interconnected circulating fluidised bed reactors

reference_plants.name: La Pereda pilot
reference_plants.status: biomass-fired calciner tests reached capture efficiencies above 99% in some periods (2024)

source.note: Energy & Fuels 2024, DOI 10.1021/acs.energyfuels.4c02472

advantages: Cheap, abundant sorbent (limestone)
High-temperature heat can be recovered for power
Synergy with cement: spent CaO is a raw material
limitations: Needs an air separation unit for the calciner
Sorbent activity decays with cycles, so make-up and purge are needed

sources.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

name: Chemical looping combustion

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: A solid metal oxide oxygen carrier circulates between an air reactor, where it picks up oxygen, and a fuel reactor, where it burns the fuel without contact with air. The fuel reactor exhaust is only CO2 and water, so CO2 is obtained by condensing the water, without an air separation unit.

suppliers.name: Research stage; no commercial licensor identified in the cited sources

advantages: Inherent CO2 separation with no air separation unit
limitations: Oxygen carrier attrition and lifetime
Solids circulation at scale not yet demonstrated commercially

name: Cryogenic carbon capture (desublimation)

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is dried and cooled to about -117 °C or colder so that CO2 freezes out (desublimes) and is separated as a solid, then melted and pumped as high-purity liquid CO2. Cold is recovered between the incoming and outgoing streams in multi-stream heat exchangers.

process_steps.name: CO2 desublimation at about -117 °C
equipment: desublimating heat exchanger or contact liquid vessel

reference_plants.name: Sugar Creek cement plant pilot
reference_plants.status: DOE project Feb 2022 to Apr 2025; target 95% capture and 95% purity

source.note: NETL 2022 Carbon Management meeting, SES presentation

advantages: Produces liquid CO2 directly, convenient for shipping
Can also remove other pollutants as they freeze out
limitations: Heavy refrigeration duty; economics depend on cold recovery
Pilot scale only

name: Direct air capture with liquid solvent (KOH and calcium loop)

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Fans push air through large contactors wetted with potassium hydroxide, which absorbs CO2 as carbonate. Calcium hydroxide in a pellet reactor transfers the carbonate to calcium carbonate pellets, which are calcined at about 900 °C in an oxygen-fired furnace to release concentrated CO2. The lime is slaked and returned to the loop.

performance.basis: 1 Mt/yr design, CO2 at 15 MPa, no net electricity

performance.unit: GJ/t CO2 gas plus 366 kWh/t electricity

costs.basis: 1 Mt/yr plant designs, CRF 7.5-12.5%, gas at USD 3.5/GJ; first-plant variant A 168-232

source.note: Keith et al. 2018

reference_plants.name: Squamish pilot
reference_plants.capacity: about 0.6 t/day (contactor and pellet reactor loop)

source.note: Oil & Gas Journal, 20 Jul 2023

advantages: Scales with industrial equipment (cooling-tower contactors, pulp-mill style causticising)
Location independent of emission sources
limitations: High-temperature heat needs natural gas (with its CO2 captured) or alternative heat
Cost well above point-source capture

name: Direct air capture with solid sorbent

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Fans draw air through collectors where CO2 binds to a solid sorbent. When the sorbent is saturated the collector closes and is heated to about 100 °C, releasing concentrated CO2 that is then stored. Low-temperature heat means waste or geothermal heat can be used.

process_steps.name: Desorption at about 100 °C
equipment: heating with low-grade heat or steam

process_steps.name: Storage or use
equipment: injection (e.g. mineralisation with Carbfix in Iceland)

reference_plants.name: Mammoth, Iceland
reference_plants.capacity: up to 36,000 t/yr nameplate; geothermal energy; storage by Carbfix

source.note: ESG Today, 10 May 2024

advantages: Runs on heat at about 100 °C, so geothermal or waste heat can be used
Modular
limitations: Large air volumes per tonne of CO2
Cost per tonne still high; Climeworks states costs have halved but gives no figure on the cited page

name: Emerging capture: water-lean solvents, ionic liquids and electrochemical separation

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Next-generation solvents reduce the water in the solvent, or use ionic liquids, to cut the heat needed for regeneration. Electrochemical routes release CO2 by changing the oxidation state or pH of a carrier with electricity instead of heat. The IEAGHG 2019 review rated water-lean absorbents TRL 5, ionic liquids TRL 4 and electrochemical separation TRL 4.

process_steps.name: CO2 uptake in solvent or electrochemical cell
Release by heat (lower duty) or by voltage

costs.basis: programme targets: 40 by 2025, 30 by 2030; dollar year not stated in source

source.note: NETL, Carbon Capture Technologies: Status and Challenges, January 2023

advantages: Potentially lower regeneration energy than aqueous amines
limitations: Lab to small pilot scale; long-term solvent stability and cost unproven

name: Capture from high-purity CO2 streams (compression and dehydration only)
principle: Some plants already separate CO2 as part of their process, for example acid gas removal in gas processing or fermentation in ethanol plants. Capture then only needs the CO2 to be compressed, cooled and dried to pipeline specification, which makes these the lowest-cost capture opportunities.

name: Oxyfuel combustion in cement kilns
principle: The kiln burns fuel in oxygen instead of air, and part of the exhaust is recirculated to control temperature. Without nitrogen, the exhaust is 70% CO2 or more, so it only needs purification and compression rather than a separation process.

process_steps.name: Kiln and calciner firing in O2 with flue gas recirculation

suppliers.name: European Cement Research Academy (ECRA) with Heidelberg Materials and Holcim

reference_plants.capacity: industrial scale; test phase about EUR 80 million

source.note: Heidelberg Materials page, 15 Mar 2018

advantages: Concentrated CO2 without a solvent
Can be combined with other capture routes
limitations: Air separation unit power demand
Air ingress must be minimised; kiln modifications needed

name: Physical solvent acid gas removal (pre-combustion)
principle: At high pressure and high CO2 partial pressure, organic solvents such as chilled methanol (Rectisol) or Selexol dissolve CO2 and H2S without chemical reaction. The rich solvent is depressurised in stages to release CO2, then stripped, and returned to the absorber. Physical solvents favour high-pressure syngas, while chemical solvents suit low partial pressures.

process_steps.name: Acid gas absorption at low temperature

suppliers.name: Rectisol and Selexol licensors (see NETL Gasifipedia)

advantages: Very deep sulfur removal (Rectisol below 0.1 ppmv H2S plus COS per NETL)
Low regeneration heat, since much CO2 is released by pressure let-down
limitations: Needs high pressure and high CO2 partial pressure
Refrigeration makes capital cost two to three times that of chemical solvents (NETL)

name: Polymeric membrane capture
applications: coal and gas power flue gas

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas passes over a CO2-selective polymer membrane. A pressure difference across the membrane, created by compressing the feed and/or applying vacuum on the permeate side, drives CO2 through faster than nitrogen. Multiple stages and recycle raise purity and capture rate; no chemicals or steam are needed.

process_steps.name: First membrane stage
equipment: membrane modules (spiral wound or hollow fibre)

process_steps.name: Second stage or liquefaction for purity
equipment: membrane modules or CO2 liquefaction unit

reference_plants.status: under construction in Sept 2023, slated to operate in 2024

source.note: MTR press release, 6 Sep 2023

advantages: No chemicals, little water, no steam
Modular
limitations: Power for compression and vacuum rises steeply at low CO2 concentration
Not yet proven at commercial scale on flue gas

name: Solid sorbent capture by rapid temperature swing
applications: gas and oil field steam generators

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: CO2 adsorbs onto a solid sorbent (amine-based or a metal-organic framework such as CALF-20) laid out as thin structured filters. The filters rotate through adsorption, steam regeneration and cooling zones in about a minute, so a small sorbent inventory handles a large gas flow.

process_steps.name: Adsorption on structured sorbent
equipment: rotary adsorption machine with structured filters

suppliers.name: Svante
suppliers.product: rapid cycle thermal swing adsorption with structured adsorbents

source.note: NETL project page, Dec 2021

advantages: Up to 95% capture reported, with high-purity CO2 in about 60 seconds of cycle (NETL page)
MOF sorbent (CALF-20) binds CO2 physically, lowering steam demand, and tolerates O2 and acid gases
limitations: Largest units are still engineering scale; commercial-scale references pending

name: Chemical solvent capture from syngas (hydrogen plants)
principle: In hydrogen plants, CO2 is removed from the shifted syngas at moderate pressure with an activated amine solvent before the hydrogen is purified. The CO2 is released in a regenerator and compressed. Capturing from syngas alone leaves the reformer furnace flue gas uncaptured.

reference_plants.capacity: 1 Mt/yr nameplate; about 80% of CO2 from the hydrogen units
reference_plants.status: operating; more than 3 Mt captured by early 2019

source.note: Shell white paper, February 2019

costs.basis: NETL industrial case; 99% capture 57.3; retrofit 61.7. Check the report for which streams are captured at each rate

source.note: NETL, Cost of Capturing CO2 from Industrial Sources, 15 July 2022, Exhibit ES-2 (p. 2)

advantages: Proven in hydrogen and ammonia plants
Shell cites up to 30% lower regeneration energy than accelerated MDEA for ADIP ULTRA (vendor claim)
limitations: Captures only process CO2; high capture rates also need flue gas capture on the reformer furnace
